name: Las Navas de Tolosa, Almohad Power Broken
summary: The combined Christian armies of Alfonso VIII of Castile, Peter II of Aragon, and Sancho VII of Navarre defeat the Almohad Caliph Muhammad al-Nasir at Las Navas de Tolosa in July 1212. The Almohad army of approximately 100,000 is routed; Almohad power collapses. Within three decades, Castile takes Córdoba (1236), Valencia (1238), and Seville (1248); Portugal reaches the Algarve (1249). The Reconquista accelerates dramatically.

_quarry.structural_significance: Las Navas is the decisive battle of the Iberian Reconquista; the Almohad defeat collapses the most militarily capable Islamic power in Iberia; the rapid subsequent Christian expansion (1236-1248) is the most extensive territorial change in medieval Iberia; the battle demonstrates that Iberian Christian kingdoms could unite against a common enemy despite mutual hostility, a pattern repeated in the later Crusades
